**D.** Carol likely wins because the ad's description of a 1964 Thunderbird is an express warranty that formed part of the basis of the bargain, and under UCC § 2-316(1) a generic "as is" clause cannot negate it when the two can reasonably be read together. The "as is" language disclaims only implied warranties, so the seller remains liable for the misdescribed model year. The website photo of a perfect car supports her position but is not the main ground.

CONFIDENCE: 75
